basics.description: Redeploys an EXISTING Segue install onto a new application version — the minimum-steps update path (Container Apps roll a new revision on the new image tag; FHIRBridgeDb migrates automatically on boot). This targets the SAME resource group and resources as your original install, it does not create a new environment. Postgres mode, Redis mode, and app/worker container sizes are read back from the live install and pre-filled automatically — just confirm they look right. Secrets mode and storage redundancy CANNOT be safely auto-read (Azure never exposes secret-store choice or lets a storage account's redundancy be probed reliably this way), so you still confirm those two and re-enter the Postgres password/API signing key (Azure never returns secret parameter values to anything, ever, by design). Container/database/cache SIZES for Postgres/Redis specifically are left at main.bicep's own defaults by this limited wizard — use Step 4 (upgrade-resources) or the full Deploy-to-Azure wizard if your original install customized those.

location.label: Region
location.toolTip: Must match the region your original Segue install already runs in.

basics.name: namePrefix
basics.label: Existing deployment name prefix
basics.toolTip: MUST match the prefix your original install used (e.g. <prefix>-app, <prefix>-postgres) — this is what makes this an in-place update of the existing app/worker instead of a brand-new deployment.

constraints.validationMessage: Lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only, starting with a letter.

options.text: Postgres mode and Redis mode below are pre-filled from your live install (checking the running app's own connection strings) — just confirm they're correct. Secrets mode and storage redundancy could NOT be safely auto-filled and still MUST match your original install exactly: getting secrets mode wrong deploys successfully and then the app can't find its secrets (SecretNotConfiguredException at runtime); getting storage redundancy wrong fails the deployment outright (PreflightValidationCheckFailed / StorageAccountTypeConversionNotAllowed). Check the original install's parameters (or the Portal resource list) if you're unsure of either.

elements.name: storageRedundancy
elements.label: Storage redundancy
elements.toolTip: MUST match what your original install actually has — check the storage account's Redundancy setting in the Portal (or the resourceManifest output from your original deploy) if unsure. This cannot be changed after the storage account exists; picking the wrong value fails this deployment.

elements.name: postgresMode
elements.label: Postgres deployment type
elements.toolTip: Auto-detected from the live install's connection string — confirm it's correct. Managed = Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server. Containerized = a Postgres container in this same environment.

elements.name: postgresPassword
elements.toolTip: The SAME Postgres password your original install used.

constraints.validationMessage: At least 8 characters, including upper case, lower case, and a digit.

elements.name: jwtSigningKey
elements.toolTip: The SAME API signing key your original install used — changing this invalidates every existing login session and refresh token.

elements.name: redisMode
elements.label: Redis deployment type
elements.toolTip: Auto-detected from the live install's connection string — confirm it's correct. Containerized = a Redis container in this same environment (self-signed TLS cert). Managed = Azure Managed Redis.

elements.name: redisPassword
elements.toolTip: The SAME Redis password your original install used.

elements.name: redisTrustedCertificateThumbprint
elements.label: Redis TLS certificate thumbprint
elements.toolTip: The SAME thumbprint your original install used (see generate-cert.ps1|sh).

elements.name: secretsMode
elements.label: Tenant/app secret storage
elements.toolTip: MUST match your original install. If your original install used Azure Key Vault, picking Local database here will make the app unable to find secrets that only exist in that vault (SecretNotConfiguredException at runtime) — and vice versa.

elements.name: imageTag
elements.label: Version to install
elements.toolTip: The published version tag to deploy, listed newest-first with the date each was pushed to the registry. This is the only thing this wizard changes. NOTE: this dropdown is populated by publish-deploy-artifacts.ps1|sh at publish time (from `az acr repository show-tags`) - these placeholder tokens are only ever uploaded after that substitution runs.

options.text: This wizard changes only the application version. Postgres/Redis mode and app/worker container sizes were auto-detected from your live install and are preserved as-is; secrets mode and storage redundancy on the previous step must match your original install exactly (confirm them there). Postgres/Redis-specific sizes (their own container size, or the managed SKU/storage/tier) are still left at main.bicep's own defaults — use Step 4 (upgrade-resources) or the full Deploy-to-Azure wizard if your original install customized those. WAF and Seq are also left at their defaults (both off) — if either was enabled on the original install, use the full wizard instead so it isn't silently disabled.
